stories.headline: Navi Pillay wins the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for advancing international law

sources.body:
South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa says Pillay "has served humanity with principle and the belief that the world can and should be a better place".

Pillay became the fifth South African winner of the Nobel Peace Prize - following in the footsteps of Nelson Mandela and Archbishop Desmond Tutu.

Ramaphosa describes her as a "pioneering defence attorney for anti-apartheid activists".

He adds that her win "allows us to celebrate the progressive contributions she has made to strengthen peace, uphold human dignity and bring hope in South Africa and to peoples globally".

“The honour bestowed on her reminds us to build a society where every person, whatever their circumstances, can develop their abilities and contribute fully to our nation and the world."
sources.headline: Navi Pillay, former UN human rights commissioner, wins Nobel Peace Prize

sources.body:
Committee recognises work of South African who chaired UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza

The Nobel Peace Prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza .

The Norwegian Nobel committee said Pillay, who is serving as a judge at the International Court of Justice (ICJ), has “shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence”.

“Navi Pillay’s commitment to universal legal principles and her firm moral compass are constants in a long career,” the committee said, mentioning her early work defending Nelson Mandela under South Africa’s apartheid regime, serving on international criminal tribunal, and then as the UN high commissioner for human rights, as well as chairing the UN independent international commission of inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory.

That commission concluded last year that the state of Israel was guilty of genocidal acts in Gaza “with the specific intent to destroy Palestinians in Gaza”, and said the country’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, its president, Isaac Herzog, and its former defence minister Yoav Gallant had “incited the commission of genocide”.

“It is clear that there is an intent to destroy the Palestinians in Gaza through acts that meet the criteria set forth in the genocide convention,” Pillay said on the publication of the commission’s findings in September last year.

Israel refused to cooperate with the commission, arguing it was biased, and rejected its report as “scandalous”.

In its statement , the Nobel committee said Pillay, 85, had “contributed to strengthen the institutions of international law”.

“Her independence, expertise and steadfastness have made her one of the most respected international jurists of our time,” the committee said.

“In awarding this year’s Nobel peace prize , the Norwegian Nobel committee wants to remind the world that the rule of law – national and international – underpins the system we have set up to ensure peace and resolve conflicts non-violently,” its statement said.

The committee said it had not been able to locate Pillay before its announcement on Friday morning. She was attending a meeting of human rights lawyers and jurists in Nuremberg, Germany, at the site of postwar war crimes trials of Nazi leaders, and heard the news from colleagues. She responded in disbelief.

“I don’t know about it so much. The question is: is it true? Being a lawyer and a judge, I still want to verify it,” she said.

“The last thing I did was the report on Gaza naming what’s happening there as genocide,” Pillay added. “One of the main reactions to that report was people [complimented] me for my courage. You can imagine how surprised I was. Why would you need courage to speak the truth. You interpret the law. You look at all the facts, so it’s an impartial decision.”

Pillay is currently overseeing a genocide case against Myanmar at the ICJ.
sources.headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law

sources.body:
Pillay has been instrumental in ensuring war crimes and genocide are prosecuted, Nobel committee says.

The Norwegian Nobel Committee has awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to Navanethem “Navi” Pillay.

The committee’s announcement of the 125th Nobel Peace Prize, made on Friday in Oslo, said the award would go to the South African jurist for her work to promote peace and international law.

The committee said in a statement that Pillay, a former United Nations high commissioner for human rights, had been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted.

“At a time of existential challenges – including more wars and conflicts than the world has seen in a long time – international law is no longer just a supplement to peace and security. It is an absolute necessity,” the statement read.

Committee Chairman Jorgen Watne Frydnes said the system of international law was “under tremendous pressure” and its institutions were “under attack”. It is judges, he continued, “who guard the thin red line between order and chaos”.

A South African of Indian Tamil origin, the 85-year-old Pillay was the first woman to start a law practice in what was then the province of Natal in 1967.

She was a defence lawyer for Nelson Mandela, who previously won the peace prize, and other antiapartheid activists and was the first woman of colour to serve on South Africa’s High Court.

She later served on the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court and as the UN’s rights chief.

The committee highlighted her role during her time on the Rwanda tribunal in establishing that rape and sexual violence can constitute crimes against humanity and genocide.

She chaired the UN Independent International Commission of inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory, which concluded last year that Israel committed genocide in Gaza.

“We concluded that the State of Israel is responsible for the commission of four genocidal acts in Gaza with the specific intent to destroy Palestinians in Gaza, as such,” she declared in a presentation to the UN General Assembly.

She also declared Israel’s president, prime minister and former defence minister had “incited the commission” of genocide.

She currently sits on the International Court of Justice in the case in which Myanmar stands accused of genocide against the Rohingya.

Reacting to the award, Pillay said she thought at first it must be a joke. “Being a lawyer and a judge, I still want to verify this,” she remarked.

“The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza, naming what’s happening there as genocide,” she continued. “One of the main reactions to that report is paying tribute to me for my courage. And you can imagine how surprised I was. Why would you need courage to speak the truth?”

The prize, which is worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2m), will be presented in Oslo ‌on ‌December 10 on the anniversary of the death of Swedish industrialist Alfred Nobel, who founded the awards in his 1895 will.
sources.headline: 2026 Nobel Peace Prize awarded to Navi Pillay

stories.headline: Houthi attack on Riyadh airport kills three Saudi nationals as regional war escalates

sources.body:
Attack is deadliest in kingdom since it launched major military offensive with allies against Houthis in Yemen

Three Saudi citizens have been killed and several other people were wounded in attacks targeting Riyadh ⁠airport for which Yemen’s Houthis claimed responsibility, Saudi officials have said.

The attack late on Thursday was the deadliest in Saudi Arabia since the kingdom and allied forces in neighbouring Yemen launched a major military offensive last weekend against the Iran-backed Houthis.

It was also a significant escalation in the latest front in the Iran war, which has kept oil prices and markets jumpy.

The first attack on Thursday afternoon targeted airport facilities, while the second struck aircraft, the Saudi statement said. It did not identify those responsible, though the Houthis claimed to have targeted the airport with a ballistic missile.

Among the dead was Capt Hamoud Ali Alkalthami, the Saudia Group said in a statement. It appeared to be the first confirmed attack on the Saudi national carrier since the new offensive began. A separate Saudia Group statement said one of its aircraft was damaged while it was on the ground, with no passengers onboard.

The aviation statement said the injuries to citizens and people of other nationalities “ranged from minor to serious”. The Saudia Group statement said operational activities at the airport returned to normal at 6pm on Thursday, hours after the attack.

Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had destroyed three rocket launch platforms used by the rebels to threaten regional security.

The Houthis say they are targeting the kingdom over its support for government forces in ​Yemen’s reignited civil war. Saudi Arabia says it is backing an offensive by Yemen’s UN-recognised government to ‌take back territory from the Houthis.

The Houthis have made a lightning advance across Yemen’s coastal plain over the last month, appearing to gain ground in the south-west on Wednesday as the group approached the city of Taiz.

Independent observers said earlier this week there was danger the group was on course to capture Taiz, with some signs that forces linked to the government were pulling back to secure the major port city of Aden.

Riyadh is due to host a meeting of energy policymakers, the WPC Energy Congress, this week.
sources.headline: Three Saudis killed in Riyadh airport attack claimed by Houthis

sources.body:
Rendición de 250 soldados rusos durante la 'Operación Vivaldi'. / Tercer Cuerpo del Ejército

Nunca lo dijo públicamente. Pero filtraciones gubernamentales y analistas de inteligencia habían venido asegurando en los últimos meses que el presidente Vladímir Putin se había fijado como objetivo la conquista de la totalidad del Cinturón-Fortaleza del Donbás , la línea defensiva que atravesaba cuatro grandes ciudades ucranianas y que impedía que la región entera fuera ocupada por las tropas del Kremlin. Sin embargo, cuando acaba de comenzar el otoño, el Instituto de Estudios sobre la Guerra (ISW) , el think tank más citado por medios de comunicación internacionales y analistas militares, acaba de proclamar con todo el boato que dicho esfuerzo "ha fracasado", gracias a una discreta contraofensiva ucraniana denominada 'Operación Vivaldi', que lleva meses vigente y que ha obligado a las fuerzas del Kremlin a retroceder en la zona norte del frente. Ante los reveses registrados en el campo de batalla, Rusia y sus fuerzas aéreas concentran sus esfuerzos en doblegar la resistencia ucraniana y desmoralizar a sus ciudadanos mediante bombardeos indiscriminados contra objetivos civiles que, sin ir más lejos, este jueves causaron al menos una treintena de muertos.

El denominado 'Cinturón-Fortaleza' se apoya en la existencia de cuatro ciudades de tamaño respetable situadas en línea y a una distancia relativamente corta la una de la otra: Konstantinivka , Druzhkivka , Kramatorsk y Sloviansk , conectadas por una carretera, la H-20 , y una línea de tren, y multitud de suburbios y asentamientos entre ellas. Las fuerzas ucranianas llevan reforzando esta zona de forma continua, acumulando durante más de una década trincheras , líneas de dientes de dragón, redes antidrones y zonas de fueg o preparadas. Descartado un asalto frontal con el grueso de las tropas por impracticable, y habida cuenta de que en un combate urbano, calle por calle , el bando defensor suele partir en posición de ventaja , los mandos militares rusos se habían propuesto rodear a esta línea defensiva avanzando por los flancos, es decir intentando tomar las localidades de Dobropilya en el sur y Lyman en el norte. La denominada 'Operación Vivaldi', una contraofensiva secreta que estaba siendo llevada a cabo por el 3.er Cuerpo del Ejército de Ucrania bajo el mando del general Andri Biletsky desde mayo y que solo recientemente ha sido revelada, ha acabado por arruinar estos esfuerzos.

Bautizada con el nombre del músico italiano que compuso 'Las cuatro estaciones', porque lleva desarrollándose desde la primavera hasta el otoño, ha conseguido hacer retroceder el avance ruso en la tenaza norte, recuperar para Ucrania alrededor de 200 kilómetros cuadrados de territorio, capturar entre dos y tres centenares de militares rusos y forzar la huida de otros miles. "Ha sido un gran fracaso del liderazgo político y militar ruso, tanto en el plano estratégico como en el plano táctico", ha asegurado a EL PERIÓDICO Andrii Ordynovich , director de apoyo estratégico y desarrollo en el think tank Ukranian Freedom Fund , un hombre que en el pasado ocupó cargos en la misión de Ucrania ante la OTAN y en la embajada de su país en Washington. Evitando proporcionar detalles de la misión, este analista, por contra, ha destacado la profesionalidad del Ejército de su país, que ha mantenido "silencio" hasta fecha reciente sobre una contraofensiva que considera " bien planeada y coordinada ".

stories.headline: Ethiopia launches drone strike after Eritrean troops cross into Tigray

sources.body:
Government forces’ attack raises risk of internal conflict in Ethiopia that could trigger regional war

Eritrean troops who crossed into Ethiopia’s Tigray region have come under drone attack from government forces, raising the risk that renewed internal conflict in Ethiopia could trigger an all-out regional war between the neighbouring countries.

Military vehicles carrying soldiers drove across Eritrea’s southern border into Tigray on Wednesday, reaching the town of Adigrat 25 miles (40km) south, according to civilian witnesses, a militia commander and the conflict monitoring group Acled.

Eritrean troops were then targeted by Ethiopian government drones on Wednesday evening and Thursday morning, Acled said.

Eritrea has a historical enmity with the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which launched an offensive against the Ethiopian government on 23 September, but that previous hostility has been superseded by Eritrea’s desire to head off a perceived risk of Ethiopia invading it, in order to access the Red Sea.

In the last two weeks, the TPLF and six other armed groups in Ethiopia have fought the government in Tigray and the neighbouring regions Amhara and Afar. Ethiopia’s military pushed back and an allied militia, the Tigray Peace Force, took over Tigray’s regional capital, Mekelle, on 4 October after the TPLF withdrew from the city.

Eritrea’s information minister, Yemane Ghebremeskel, said in a statement: “We are not in the business of refuting wild allegations or narratives.” He did not explicitly confirm or deny the presence of Eritrean troops in Ethiopia.

Ethiopia’s foreign ministry said in a statement on Monday: “Ethiopia stands ready to defend its sovereignty, territorial integrity, and core national interests, while urging all regional actors to address shared challenges through constructive dialogue, partnership, and adherence to the principles of good neighbourliness rather than confrontation and zero-sum approaches.”

The TPLF and Ethiopia’s government fought a brutal civil war from 2020 to 2022. Between 300,000 and 800,000 civilians died , according to British government estimates. Both sides and their allies were accused of war crimes.

Eritrea intervened on the side of Ethiopia in that conflict, after a rapprochement between the two countries in 2018, which earned Ethiopia’s prime minister, Abiy Ahmed, the 2019 Nobel peace prize .

Eritrea, which gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, has a long enmity with the TPLF, which ruled Ethiopia from 1991 to 2018. The two countries fought a war from 1998 to 2000.

Relations between the countries have deteriorated again in recent years. Abiy has said Ethiopia needs access to the Red Sea, and state media has claimed the country has historical rights to the Eritrean port of Assab. The US-Israeli war on Iran – leading Iran to limit shipping through the strait of Hormuz – has further raised the stakes of Red Sea access.

In its statement on Monday, Ethiopia’s foreign ministry said: “Any serious discussion of regional maritime affairs and security architecture must account for Ethiopia’s legitimate interests and its enduring connection to the Red Sea.”
sources.headline: Ethiopia launches drone attack against Eritrean troops who crossed into Tigray

sources.body:
Tigray’s renewed war is testing Ethiopia’s already strained regional ties.

Addis Ababa, Ethiopia – After nearly two weeks of fierce fighting, Ethiopian federal forces entered the Tigrayan capital of Mekelle as forces from an alliance of rebel groups, including the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), withdrew from the city.

The fighting that erupted late last month has effectively ended the 2022 Pretoria ceasefire and the fragile peace that followed the devastating Tigray war.

But Mekelle’s capture may mark the end of conventional warfare rather than the end of the conflict. Fighting has continued elsewhere in Tigray, while reports of Eritrean troops entering northern Tigrayan towns have added a potentially more dangerous regional dimension.

Ethiopian federal forces used air power and ground forces to advance across Tigray. After suffering successive defeats around the towns of Alamata and Kobo, rebel forces withdrew into the surrounding countryside. They have pledged to continue fighting.

“We will confront the enemy on our terms and where we choose,” TPLF leader Debretsion Gebremichael said.

There are echoes of the war that began in 2020, when Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government declared victory after federal forces captured Mekelle. Tigrayan forces subsequently regrouped in the mountains, retook much of the region and recaptured the capital, prolonging the war for nearly a year and a half.

The renewed conflict could follow a similar trajectory, particularly if the TPLF and other armed groups succeed in turning the mountainous terrain into a prolonged armed rebellion. Ethiopia is already fighting insurgencies in Amhara and Oromia, raising the prospect of its federal forces being stretched across multiple fronts.

But the battlefield reversals suffered by the rebels could have implications well beyond Tigray. They have raised concern in Egypt and among other Ethiopian rivals, according to Hossamaldeen Ibrahim, an African analyst at the Bloomsbury Intelligence and Security Institute.

“Egypt views the Renaissance Dam, and any Ethiopian [army] move towards the Red Sea, as a strategic threat, so it has allied with Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia against any Ethiopian unilateralism,” Ibrahim told Al Jazeera.

“Ethiopia is seeking a sea outlet; Eritrea sees this as an existential threat.”

Ethiopia has been landlocked since Eritrea won its war of independence in 1991, leaving Addis Ababa heavily dependent on neighbouring countries for access to international trade.

Abiy has increasingly made access to the Red Sea a strategic priority since 2023, raising concerns in Eritrea over Ethiopia’s ambitions, particularly over the port of Assab.

Ethiopia currently relies heavily on Djibouti for maritime trade, while also pursuing alternative arrangements, including through Kenya and Somaliland.

After being sworn in on Monday for another five-year term following his party’s victory in the June 1 election, Abiy again put the issue at the centre of his parliamentary address.

“Based on the principle of give and take, we will work diligently to ensure that Ethiopia has an outlet to the sea,” he told parliament.
sources.headline: Will Ethiopia’s neighbours intervene as Tigray war escalates?

stories.headline: Hurricane Isaias becomes the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season

sources.body:
Storm expected to make landfall on US’s northern Gulf coast with risk of flash floods and isolated river flooding

Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

As a result of the strong El Niño , it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season. The first hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 8 October 1905, which pre-dates the satellite era (1960s) for tracking hurricanes that has allowed for more non-landfall hurricanes to be discovered.

Isaias is expected to make landfall on Friday evening local time, bringing an estimated 75-150mm (2.9-5.9in) of rainfall across the Gulf coast. There may be up to 250mm in places, with a possibility of flash flooding and isolated river flooding.

The NOAA also said there was increasing likelihood of life-threatening storm surge along portions of the northern Gulf coast and damaging hurricane-force winds over portions of the Florida panhandle, southern Alabama and Mississippi . A hurricane warning has been issued and people have been told to prepare for long power outages and to obey any evacuation orders issued.

In Zimbabwe , a state of disaster was declared in the south-east Masvingo province on Tuesday after a severe hailstorm caused widespread damage to homes and critical infrastructure.

Preliminary assessments found the roofs had been torn off 8,500 homes. A further 15,300 people reported shattered windows, leaving many exposed to the elements as the rainy season begins.

The country’s power infrastructure was badly affected, disrupting drainage and sewerage systems, raising concerns about public health.

In Australia, a rare tornado hit the town of Ulladulla, about 140 miles (230km) south of Sydney, on 3 October. Tornadoes are relatively rare in Australia, where there are about 50 each year. This Ulladulla tornado damaged properties and felled trees.
sources.headline: Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season

sources.headline: ICE officer shoots, wounds man in car on crowded New York street

sources.body: US immigration agents shot and wounded a man on Thursday in ​his car with a child present in the Marble Hill neighborhood of New York City, according to the mayor, city police and eyewitnesses. Federal immigration agents have shot at least 21 people since Republican President Donald Trump returned to office, 7 fatally, sparking protests across ​the US.
sources.headline: New York City man shot in car with child present by ICE agents, mayor says

sources.body:
Mayor Zohran Mamdani says immigration agents fire at car with child inside. DHS says man was an arrest target.

An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent has shot a man in New York City as he sat in a car with a child.

Citing an “unconscionable and incredibly serious situation”, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said early reports indicated that agents surrounded the man and a five-year-old in his car on Thursday in the Marble Hill neighbourhood before firing multiple rounds.

The child was believed to be physically unharmed, the mayor added as he said he has called United States President Donald Trump and would demand that he end all ICE enforcement actions in the city.

“I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorise our communities,” Mamdani said.

Protests followed on Thursday evening with demonstrators saying the shooting illustrated the dangers of Trump’s immigration crackdown, and some scuffles with police broke out.

“We are heartbroken and enraged,” said City Council member Carmen De La Rosa, who represents the area.

Speaking at the scene in the evening, Mamdani said: “Today’s shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known, which is that ICE operates with impunity, that they sow chaos and terror across our country, that they have killed far more of our neighbours than they could ever have claimed to save.”

He demanded the agency “must be abolished”.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul said she spoke with Trump and US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Thursday night.

“I expressed outrage on behalf of New Yorkers and urged them to halt ICE enforcement operations in New York,” she said in a statement.

“I also asked that any body camera footage of the shooting be released to the public, so we can establish the facts and get to the truth.”

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, said its officers were conducting a “targeted enforcement operation” in the Bronx about 4pm to arrest a 28-year-old Dominican national with a criminal conviction identified as Oscar Belgal by city police.

It said an officer “discharged his weapon” and “the criminal illegal alien” was injured. The DHS added that the incident remains under investigation.

Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said Belgal was pulling into a parking space when a federal officer in plain clothes approached with a gun drawn, followed by another federal officer who also wasn’t in uniform.

Belgal started to pull the car forward, and then at least one of the officers fired seven rounds, hitting the man below his left ear, Tisch said, confirming that the child was unharmed and was with a relative.

According to a statement by the New York Police Department, the man remained conscious and was receiving medical treatment at a nearby hospital.

The shooting took place after months of mounting criticism of the agency.

In January, federal immigration agents shot dead two US citizens in Minneapolis: Renee Nicole Good, a 37-year-old mother of three, killed by an ICE agent on January 7, and Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old intensive care nurse, shot by a US border agent.

sources.headline: Trump officials block Microsoft’s access to program for employee green cards

sources.body: The Trump administration continues to crack down on immigration, with new restrictions on the H-1B visa programme. US Vice President JD Vance singled out Microsoft as having abused the system to recruit low-cost foreign workers, to the detriment of the American workforce. The tech giant has defended its hiring practices. Also in the show: Germany could join a UK-led fighter jet development programme, months after pulling out of a joint French project.
sources.headline: US targets Microsoft, Adobe in new visa crackdown

sources.body:
The US is suspending top tech firms, including Microsoft, from a key programme to sponsor foreign workers’ green cards.

The United States government has moved to exclude some of the world’s top tech companies from a programme that allows them to sponsor skilled foreign workers for permanent residency.

Vice President JD Vance said the action was a response to companies abusing the system to hire lower-paid foreign workers at the expense of US workers.

It comes as US President Donald Trump’s administration continues efforts to clamp down on immigration – both legal and undocumented – and make it harder for immigrants to get residency or citizenship.

But the latest move also potentially impacts thousands of foreign workers, many of whom have spent years waiting for a backlog in applications to clear.

Here’s what to know about the latest policy:

The suspension concerns the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme, which enables a US-based employer to sponsor a foreign worker’s green card — as the permanent residency is commonly known. To qualify, the employer is supposed to demonstrate that there are insufficient US workers for a needed job role and that bringing a foreign worker will not impact the pay or conditions of US workers in the industry.

PERM is a key step in the green card process for many skilled foreign workers. Major tech companies often hire workers on temporary visas, such as the H-1B, before they transition to permanent residency through the PERM process.

Vance on Thursday accused major companies of fraudulently using the current visa regime to displace US employees and bring in lower-paid foreign workers who amount to “indentured servants”.

“The programme has become rife with fraud,” said Vance at a White House news conference. He claimed that many workers who start off on temporary H-1B visas and later apply for permanent residency under the PERM programme are “being mistreated by their employers” and “used to undercut the wages of American workers”.

“You’ve got to hire great American workers,” the US vice president said. “You cannot lay off American workers and then replace them with foreign indentured servants.”

Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling used similar language, saying the US would “shut down the pipeline of systemic fraud that has flooded our country”.

“The fraud doesn’t end with getting the job,” said Sonderling. “That job becomes a pathway for foreign workers and their families to stay in America permanently and eventually (become) US citizens.”

“And who pays for it all? The American worker,” he said.

Vance singled out Microsoft as a major offender and said it would be suspended from the PERM programme.

Other companies whose PERM applications will no longer be processed include US software firm Adobe and some of the world’s top IT firms, including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini. Of these, Capgemini is French, Microsoft and Adobe are American, and the rest — Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro and HCL — are all Indian.
sources.headline: ‘Indentured servants’: US green card move will hit thousands of IT workers

stories.headline: Pentagon says it will livestream firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan

sources.body:
The public will be able to watch the execution of a former US Army major by firing squad, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has said.

A Defense Department official told the BBC the execution of Nidal Hasan, who shot dead 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, would be livestreamed.

It is believed it would be the first public execution in the US in almost a century. The decision to livestream it is "unprecedented in the modern era" and "on uncertain legal terrain," said John Mills, a lawyer who works with inmates sentenced to death.

"People need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things," said Hegseth.

The UN human rights office told AFP that livestreaming it would be "tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture".

Democratic Senator Chris Murphy told CNN that the idea was "disgusting" and reminiscent of executions carried out by the Islamic State group.

The Pentagon announced earlier this week it would execute Hasan in the first military execution in more than 60 years.

Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist from Virginia, admitted fatally shooting 13 unarmed soldiers in a crowded medical building at Fort Hood.

Alonzo Lunsford, a former US Army sergeant who was shot seven times in the attack, told the BBC's Today programme that he supported the execution by firing squad, as a method "befitting" for what he did.

He does not believe everyone should be able to watch the livestream, concerned about the message it sends younger people, but says it is important that those affected by the shooting are given the opportunity.

"As far as the families of the fallen and the families of the survivors, and the survivors themselves, yes, I think we should be able to look at it uncensored."

Lunsford says he plans to attend the execution and before they pull the trigger he wants Hasan to look him in the eyes. "I want him to know he failed. I'm still here."

Hegseth said in an interview with conservative TV outlet Real America's Voice that Hasan is "gonna get a firing squad of soldiers. As it should be".

Asked if Hasan had made any final requests or reached out to President Donald Trump, Hegseth said: "Don't care. We'll see him on December 3rd."

A Pentagon spokesperson said on Monday that Trump had approved the defence secretary's recommendation. The BBC has asked the White House whether Trump supports a livestreamed public execution.

While there were more than 2,700 executions across 17 countries last year, only two countries carried them out publicly.

Eleven public executions were known to have been carried out in Iran in 2025, and another six in Afghanistan, according to Amnesty International.

The execution is scheduled to take place at Fort Hood in Texas on 3 December. It will be the first military execution by firing squad since the end of World War Two.

In court Hasan apologised for "any mistakes". He said during his court martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan.

La ejecución por pelotón de fusilamiento del autor del tiroteo en Fort Hood, Nidal Malik Hasan , será retransmitida en directo, según ha anunciado este jueves el Pentágono, en una sorprendente revelación sobre los planes para la primera ejecución militar en más de 65 años, tras las declaraciones del secretario de Defensa Pete Hegseth, que había anunciado que el acto será “público”.

El Ejército anunció esta semana que la ejecución tendrá lugar en Fort Hood el 3 de diciembre, después de que Hasan fuera condenado por el asesinato de 13 personas y de causar heridas a otras 32 durante un tiroteo en la base militar en 2009.

Hegseth, que intervino en el canal conservador Real America’s Voice el miércoles, afirmó: “Nos aseguraremos de que la gente pueda verlo, que sea público”.

Funcionarios del Pentágono aclararon el jueves que la ejecución se retransmitirá en directo y que se proporcionarán más detalles próximamente.La revelación de Hegseth sobre la naturaleza pública de la ejecución -y aún más en una modalidad tan violenta como el pelotón de fusilamiento- ha suscitado nuevas cuestiones sobre la aplicación de la pena de muerte en Estados Unidos, especialmente tras la fallida inyección letal de Christa Pike en Tennessee .

Hasan podría intentar resistirse a la ejecución y presentar un recurso de habeas corpus -una solicitud legal para revisar la legalidad de una detención- en un tribunal civil, lo cual podría retrasar considerablemente la ejecución, según expertos consultados.

“Francamente, podría prolongarse más allá de la actual administración, y quién sabe si la próxima tendrá el mismo afán por ejecutar sentencias”, opina Eugene R. Fidell, profesor visitante en la Facultad de Derecho de Yale y especialista en derecho militar.

Deborah Denno, experta en pena de muerte y profesora de derecho en la Universidad de Fordham, señala que retransmitir una ejecución en directo podría hacer el proceso “mucho más transparente” y servir para informar al público sobre todo lo que implica la pena capital. Desde su punto de vista, estos beneficios serían útiles precisamente ahora, cuando la ejecución fallida de Pike ha renovado las dudas sobre el modo en que los condenados son ejecutados por sus delitos. “Creo que podría ser una buena idea porque se haría de forma transparente y el público sería plenamente consciente de que está ocurriendo”, afirma.

A medida que muchos estados se encuentran con dificultades para llevar a cabo ejecuciones mediante inyección letal, debido a la falta de acceso a fármacos o a la negativa de profesionales médicos a participar, el pelotón de fusilamiento empieza a verse como una alternativa menos inhumana, asegura Brenner Fissell, profesor de derecho en Villanova y vicepresidente del Instituto Nacional de Justicia Militar. “Hay una percepción de masculinidad y de carácter militar asociada al pelotón de fusilamiento que forma parte del aura que Hegseth intenta destacar, la llamada ‘cultura de la letalidad’”.

Elisabeth Semel, codirectora de la Clínica sobre la Pena de Muerte en la Facultad de Derecho de UC Berkeley, apunta que el anuncio de Hegseth plantea una serie de cuestiones legales y de política pública, incluidas preocupaciones sobre la dignidad del acusado, sobre quién podría asistir a la ejecución y sobre las intenciones de la administración Trump al optar por un espectáculo tan poco habitual. Aunque se ha debatido largamente la posibilidad de televisar una ejecución, “no recuerdo un caso en el que la iniciativa viniera del Gobierno. Eso también plantea serias dudas sobre cuáles son las motivaciones del Gobierno”, señala. “Este es un presidente centrado en el espectáculo y creo que precisamente ese es el mensaje que intenta transmitir”, añade Semel, quien se muestra escéptica sobre si la administración ha considerado los problemas legales y sociales que implica esta decisión.

stories.headline: Republicans fear losses in traditionally safe House seats as the midterms approach

sources.body: In late September, top Republicans across House GOP leadership, leading political operations and individual campaigns received a trove of internal polling. It sparked a new level of panic. The polling didn’t just reveal a harsh environment for the party in power on par with typical midterms, but rather some close-to-catastrophic scenarios in a slew of formerly safe red seats across the country, according to three people with direct knowledge of the matter who were granted anonymity to discuss private information. Key seats in Kentucky, North Carolina, Nevada and other areas that President Donald Trump won by 10 points or more in 2024 were competitive. All three vulnerable GOP-held seats in Iowa looked doomed. And most ominously, a crop of Republican incumbents who haven’t had to run serious races in years were vulnerable, from Oklahoma to Wisconsin and beyond. Now, less than four weeks before Election Day, the concerns are running so deep and the atmosphere is so uncertain that Republicans are beginning to brace for some of the worst-case scenarios. "Polls aren't looking good,” retiring Rep. Barry Loudermilk (R-Ga.) said in an interview. “But we've also seen in the past couple of cycles, polls are really hard to predict. I think there's just a lot of things in play, and of course, what do we have three weeks out — that's light years in political time.” One senior House Republican involved in the conversations added: “I think the scary part is we don’t know where the bottom is.” They, like others in this report, were granted anonymity to discuss the political climate honestly. Their worst fear — according to conversations with more than two dozen Republican lawmakers and senior operatives — is that white working class voters in some states who have become central to the GOP coalition won’t just stay home next month, but instead they’ll be so angry or disillusioned by high fuel prices and the war in Iran that enough of them will vote for Democrats. “The environment has a lot people scared to death,” said one GOP operative working on a red-leaning House race that is competitive. “Where is the surge in Dem votes coming from?” that operative asked. “Is it truly no turnout among white working class? It's such an open question and we just don't know the answer. It's impossible.” Spokespeople for the National Republican Congressional Committee and the Republican National Committee brushed off the concerns. "Anonymous strategists who spend more time bed-wetting to media than working in the trenches to win races have no idea what they're talking about,” RNC spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre said. NRCC spokesperson Mike Marinella agreed: “House Republicans have a more favorable map, a stronger ground game, a historic fundraising and spending advantages, and battle-tested incumbents while Democrats are stuck dragging their unelectable socialist nominees across the finish line.” Still, top Republicans’ travel schedule reveals the extent of their concerns: Johnson is heading to deep-red Kentucky on Friday for a fundraiser to boost Republican Ralph Alvarado in the 6th District, which Trump won by 15 points in 2024. Johnson and Trump are also both planning trips to Montana where Republicans are working to fend off a Democratic challenger in a district the president won by more than 11 points. “Speaker Johnson is leaving it all on the field and leaving no stone unturned as he campaigns in more than 40 districts and over 20 states in the month leading up to the election,” Johnson’s spokesperson Greg Steele said. And, pointing to Johnson’s record-setting third quarter funding, Steele added that: “Johnson is not slowing down and helping to get resources to every district that will decide the majority.” Trump is holding a rally in deep-red Tennessee on Saturday, in GOP Rep. Matt Van Epps’ district. That seat — which is still considered generally safe — and several others in the state have not been on Republicans’ radar at all, but the current drag of the war and other factors are just too big for them to be comfortable. “I’m worried about all three in the area,” one Tennessee Republican said of the red-leaning districts Democrats are targeting. “Too many unknowns.” Even as internal GOP data shows a series of troubles, Republicans argue the polls are overemphasizing Democrats’ advantage. “I think there’s no question there is some undersampling,” said one RNC official, granted anonymity to discuss internal deliberations. “I’m not surprised any of these are close. I’m not surprised that Democrats are trying to make it seem like we’re on defense everywhere,” they said. “These are never [races] that we assumed were overall slam dunks, but I very much like where we sit in all of them.” Still, the person added that RNC officials don’t have their “heads in the sand” about the challenges, even as they have a more optimistic view of the map. Loudermilk pointed to Republicans’ lack of cohesive messaging on high gas prices and other goods: “I don’t know if we’re doing a good enough job doing that.” “It’s not the best of environments,” Rep. Morgan Griffith (R-Va.) told reporters in late September, though he still maintained the GOP will keep House control. “I liked it a lot better when I first got elected in 2010, when the environment was much better for Republicans.” Top Republicans are most worried about staunching the bleeding in key Midwest districts. Senior Republicans believe their internal polling, if it holds, shows likely losses across all three at-risk GOP seats in Iowa: Reps. Zach Nunn and Mariannette Miller-Meeks and the race to replace now-Senate candidate Ashley Hinson, according to four people with direct knowledge of the private information. A White House official, granted anonymity to candidly discuss the races, said the “doom and gloom notion” among the Iowa seats isn’t a new phenomenon. “But I do think that they’re probably performing better than most think that they are. And I think that folks will be pleasantly surprised [when] we go into November 3.” But benchmarks they’re watching across the larger region are deteriorating as well. Wisconsin Rep. Bryan Steil, the House Administration chair, is in a tighter than comfortable race after winning by 11 points in 2024 — as is Rep. Brad Finstad across the border in Minnesota, who won his district by 12 points 2024. In Michigan, the party has a host of problems in battleground districts, but now feels that once-safer seat Republicans — like Bill Huizenga, who Johnson campaigned with Wednesday, and the race to replace Rep. John James, who is running for governor — are in jeopardy. Similarly, after top GOP outside groups cut bait on the blue-leaning Nebraska district held by retiring Rep. Don Bacon, Republicans in the state turned their attention to Rep. Mike Flood’s seat, which Trump carried by 12 points. One silver lining for Republicans in safer red seats is many are digging in now to shore up their races, and aren’t sleepwalking to November. The White House official said it’s Trump’s “coalition of voters” that Republicans need to turn out in the midterms, and “the president is on the road almost every night this month … communicating with those individuals.” But Democrats continue to stretch further into red territory while forecasting big wins. “We feel confident that we will get to 218,” Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee political director Brooke Butler said in an interview earlier this week , saying the party could win as many as 240 seats. “The question that I’ve told people from the beginning cycle is ‘How much?’” But while Democrats are increasingly bullish, they are navigating their own tough decisions because of Republicans’ massive cash advantage , leaving the GOP optimistic they can hold a few seats where Democrats don’t have the resources to compete. Top GOP House operatives remain confident about a number of core battleground districts — including where candidates have already put some distance between themselves and Trump. One national party operative remained hopeful that as Election Day nears, the races will get closer than polling currently suggests, as has been the case in past cycles. That would help them hold some of these redder seats that are competitive. Even as Republicans hope some red seats fall off the board as Election Day nears, many operatives told POLITICO they’re worried that outside groups will have to start siphoning resources into red areas to shore them up, moving important dollars out of the battlegrounds. “People that are in R+10 districts are showing [polling that] they’re tied and they're saying, ‘I need help,’” said a GOP operative working on a battleground House race. “There's real opportunity for Democrats in a lot of these.” Rep. French Hill, the chair of the Financial Services Committee from deep-red Arkansas whose opponent was just added to the DCCC’s “Red to Blue” list, said in a recent interview with POLITICO that he considers “the atmosphere a very tough political environment right now because of President [Donald] Trump’s lack of favorability at the top, and you know people are concerned about, as I say, what it’s like to live under an inflated economy the last four years.” Johnson, an eternal optimist, made clear during a campaign stop in Pennsylvania this week that he believes “this will be a close election.” He’s ramping up his warnings across the campaign trail of what Democrats winning power would mean: “They would try to impeach the president, of course, immediately …They’d spend every waking hour investigating the president, his family, and the cabinet, and leaders of business and industry. That would roil the markets. Just ask yourself, if you're a hardworking family, how would that be for your family? That Democrats turned Congress into lawfare on steroids.” Samuel Benson contributed to this report.
sources.headline: House Republicans are bracing for catastrophe in once safe red seats

sources.body: One in four Trump voters say GOP candidates should break with the president to win in November, according to the latest POLITICO Poll , conducted by independent firm PF Global. The findings underscore the degree to which even loyal Republicans understand President Donald Trump is a drag on the ticket. Persistent inflation, $4 gas prices, 7% mortgage rates, a quagmire in the Middle East and a trade war with Canada have given Republican candidates no shortage of opportunities to take the president to task. Michigan’s GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers this week became the latest example when he called for an end to the “tariff war” with Canada — a notable shift after he spent weeks defending the president’s decision. “It was brilliant by Mike Rogers … when you talk about the affordability issue, in every poll I get back, every week, more and more people have this as their top issue,” said Michigan-based GOP consultant Jason Roe, who is working on Rep. Tom Barrett’s (R-Mich.) reelection campaign. “Obviously the price of gas is a result of the Iran war, and in Michigan, more than anything else, the trade war with Canada.” Rogers is hardly the only example. Florida GOP Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar used an ad filmed in front of the White House to call out the president’s immigration crackdown. Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa), in her bid to win the Iowa Senate seat, has called for an end to the Iran war amid souring diesel costs. Ken Paxton, the GOP’s embattled Texas Senate nominee, has now been the subject of four leaks exposing his private attempts to distance himself from Trump and the national party. “It’s just all dictated by the data,” said a GOP strategist working on a Senate campaign, granted anonymity to speak candidly about the president. “They see the writing on the wall about the gas prices and the inflation. Running as a Trump sycophant is not going to work in 2026. It’s the only political move you can do in Michigan, a state like that. It’s toxic to be tied to the man.” There are some limits: No Republican has completely broken with Trump, and several are eager to stand next to him on stage or in the Oval. Few dare to criticize him directly. And many still lean on their ties to the president on the campaign trail and in their social media profiles as they seek to rally the MAGA base. A White House official, granted anonymity to discuss internal thinking, scoffed at the idea that Rogers’ — or any other candidates’ — efforts to distance themselves from Trump administration policies, amounted to a major break with the president. “If I’m a candidate that’s physically trying to push away from the president, I’m not attending this stuff. I’m just gonna back away all the way,” the official said. “Being in the midst of a campaign and needing to talk to the issues that are being discussed as kitchen table topics, you just kind of have to.” White House spokesperson Davis Ingle pointed to the Trump administration’s efforts to lower prescription drug costs, cut taxes, secure the border and grow job numbers: “No one can dispute the fact that President Trump has created one of the most robust coalitions in political history with the MAGA movement, and the president understands how to communicate with them. President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party, and he is committed to maintaining Republican majorities in Congress.” Politicians touting their independence from Washington is nothing new. But as the poll reveals, it’s notable that so many who voted for Trump, who has been the GOP's dominant force for a decade, are ready for candidates to take that leap. Much of the fracture is driven by the non-MAGA wing of his coalition, the people who voted for Trump in 2024 but do not identify as part of his most loyal base, the survey found. When asked about specific issues such as the economy, trade and tariffs, data centers, immigration and the Iran war, non-MAGA Trump voters were roughly twice as likely as MAGA Trump voters to say their GOP candidate should break from the president. But Trump still retains an intense hold over the base. More than two-thirds of MAGA voters said GOP candidates should continue to align with Trump across all of those issues. That creates a no-win situation for many Republican candidates: Tie yourself to Trump and his policies too tightly and you lose independents and non-MAGA Republicans. Break too far, and you risk leaving MAGA disenchanted. Candidates trying to thread that needle are quick to praise the president but blame his advisers, as Salazar did, or avoid mentioning Trump by name at all. Roe said each candidate has to measure the “downstream effects” of a decision to distance themselves from the president, adding that it’s a balance between “alienating your base with appealing to voters that are looking for some independence.” On the campaign trail, many Republicans acknowledge that the president remains an asset in shoring up base voters crucial to November. It’s part of the reason Trump has aggressively traveled to red states — including Alabama, Alaska, Iowa, Nebraska, Ohio and Texas — bastions of conservatism that need his star power to coax die-hard supporters to the polls. The White House official pointed to the president’s rally with South Carolina Senate candidate Darline Graham ahead of her run-off as an example of Trump’s ability to juice turnout. RNC press secretary Natalie Baldassarre insisted that Republicans “remain united behind the president’s agenda” and are “laser focused on winning.” “Our candidates will run the races necessary to best represent their districts and prevent Democrats from taking control,” she said. The president is telling voters to “pretend” he is on the ballot, and he has insisted the party is already in a better place as he blitzes states across the country, touting his economy and arguing that higher prices are a small price to pay for national security amid the lingering war with Iran. But some candidates are still nervous that if they campaign beside the president, they could alienate undecided voters. Some Republicans have encouraged Trump’s team not to send the president to a blue-leaning Omaha district and other key districts where his approval rating is underwater ahead of Election Day. “I don’t think there are that many candidates who are clamoring for Trump to come to their state. But to the extent they do, it’s a gamble that they’ve already lost the voters who are gonna vote against them, and they need to light a fire under the voters who are sitting it out, and he’s the torch,” said Democratic strategist David Axelrod, who was chief strategist for Barack Obama’s 2008 campaign. “The problem is the torch can burn the whole house down.” The damned-if-you-do, damned-if-you-don’t dilemma is perhaps best captured with Paxton’s campaign in Texas. On Wednesday, Trump took the stage in San Antonio, bringing up Paxton, the same day his latest closed-door comments complaining about the Iran war and high prices dragging down his campaign went public. But standing on stage with Trump, he struck a much different tune. “Wow, what is it like to be up on stage with the president of the United States? Pretty amazing,” he said. “Mr. President, I want to thank you for coming for me, for coming for us and for coming for Texas.”

Félix Bolaños, entrevistado por Jordi Basté en el mon a RAC1 

“Tengo la convicción de que, si la mayoría del Parlamento da la espalda a la ciudadanía, la ciudadanía debe elegir un nuevo Parlamento. Necesitamos un Parlamento con una mayoría diferente, mucho más amplia, y esa es la razón de ser de la convocatoria electoral”, advirtió Pedro Sánchez el pasado martes, tras anunciar el día anterior el adelanto de las elecciones generales al próximo 29 de noviembre. El presidente del Gobierno busca así una nueva mayoría progresista en el Congreso, pero también en el Senado, donde la mayoría absoluta del Partido Popular ha impuesto en los mandatos de Sánchez vetos presupuestarios, bloqueos en la renovación de órganos constitucionales como el Consejo General del Poder Judicial (CGPJ), la reprobación constante de ministros, y un sinfín de comisiones de investigación para exprimir los escándalos de presunta corrupción que salpican al PSOE.

Ante la convocatoria del 29-N, no obstante, la dirección del PSOE se ha abierto a explorar fórmulas para tratar de evitar una reedición de esta mayoría absoluta del PP en el Senado, como es la presentación de candidaturas conjuntas con otras formaciones a su izquierda, para poder ampliar su representación en la Cámara Alta, según confirman a La Vanguardia fuentes socialistas y de otros partidos que están analizando esta opción.

Las negociaciones entre el PSOE y otros grupos de izquierda están en sus primeros pasos, y están plagadas de dificultades, pero ya han arrancado, según estas fuentes, con la premura además de la precipitación electoral. Aunque es precisamente la inminencia de las elecciones del 29-N lo que ha vuelto a poner sobre la mesa la necesidad de tratar de articular esta fórmula de candidaturas unitarias para rentabilizar los votos y aumentar la representación de las formaciones progresistas en el Senado. Existe un reciente precedente exitoso, en las últimas elecciones generales del 2023: el PSOE, Sumar, Esquerra Unida y Ara Eivissa sumaron fuerzas en Ibiza y Formentera con una candidatura conjunta, y lograron arrebatar un senador al PP. La intención es empezar por determinar a cuántas circunscripciones electorales se podría extender esta fórmula para que surtiera efecto el objetivo: podrían ser hasta 30. La prioridad ahora sería Madrid, y en otros territorios casi se da por seguro que se alcance un acuerdo, por ejemplo en Baleares.

La iniciativa de impulsar listas conjuntas de izquierdas al Senado cuenta además con sustento académico, político y social. Precisamente el pasado martes, cuando Sánchez defendió desde la Moncloa la necesidad de lograr en las urnas del 29-N un Parlamento diferente, con mayorías progresistas más amplias, se presentó en el Ateneo de Madrid la plataforma “Senadores y senadoras por la democracia”, que lanzó en sociedad su propuesta para que las candidaturas electorales unitarias de formaciones de izquierda logren revertir la mayoría absoluta del PP en la Cámara Alta. Según sus promotores, ya están manteniendo contactos con el PSOE, Movimiento Sumar, Izquierda Unida, Podemos, Más Madrid y Compromís.

sources.headline: Feijóo acepta un debate cara a cara con Sánchez y otro a cuatro con el resto de candidatos

sources.body:
El líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo da una rueda de prensa tras la Junta Directiva Nacional del Partido Popular celebrada este jueves en la sede del partido de la calle Génova en Madrid. 

La campaña electoral arranca el 13 de noviembre y se prolongará durante dos semanas, donde los debates van a tener un gran peso. En este sentido, Alberto Núñez Feijóo ha tomado la iniciativa y ha planteado ya un cara a cara a Pedro Sánchez  en Mediaset. Además, propone un debate con todos los candidatos y asegura que el PP participará en otro con los portavoces de los grupos políticos con representación parlamentaria.

La idea del PP es que, siguiendo el calendario de la última campaña de las elecciones generales, ese cara a cara de Feijóo y Sánchez en Mediaset se celebre el primer lunes de campaña y, por tanto, quedaría para el 16 de noviembre. Mediaset ya ha hecho una propuesta al respecto.

También existe una invitación de Atresmedia para hacer un debate con todos los candidatos -PP, PSOE, Vox, Frente Amplio...-, algo que los populares creen que debería celebrarse lo más cerca posible del día de las votaciones: por tanto, el jueves 26 de noviembre.

Finalmente, el PP participará en un debate con los portavoces de los grupos políticos con representación parlamentaria ya que existe una propuesta por parte de RTVE para el lunes 23 de noviembre. Según fuentes del PP, ahí acudirá Ester Muñoz como representante del partido.

“La campaña electoral de las elecciones generales es una fantástica oportunidad para confrontar modelos entre la España que viene y la España que se va”, señalan en las filas del PP, que apuntan a que el PP ha recibido “innumerables propuestas de entrevistas y debates de medios de comunicación y de canales alternativos”.

Más allá de los debates, Feijóo también está dispuesto a aceptar una entrevista en RTVE, aunque pone condiciones con la televisión pública en un momento en que hay muchas críticas por la vinculación con las posiciones de Sánchez. Feijóo “valorará su asistencia por respeto a la Corporación y a sus trabajadores” pese a la “innegable parcialidad y sumisión a los intereses” y a las “necesidades” del presidente del Gobierno. En este sentido, Feijóo asistirá con la “condición de que la entrevista se desarrolle en un espacio de producción propia”.

“La Compañía no tiene directivos que trabajen pensando en el interés general, pero sí magníficos profesionales de la comunicación. Deben ser ellos y no una productora externa quienes asuman del reto y la responsabilidad de organizar estas entrevistas, tan importantes, tanto en TVE como en RNE. Si RTVE cumple con esta premisa, Feijóo, irá”, resume el PP.

Fuentes del PP señalan que no se veta a ningún presentador de televisión -ni tampoco ninguno de los que desarrolla su actividad a través de productora externa, como Jesús Cintora-, pero la entrevista se debe de desarrollar en espacio de producción propia.

Asimismo, en el partido de Feijóo se muestran sorprendidos de que, horas después de la propuesta de debates, el equipo de campaña del presidente del Gobierno “aún no haya confirmado la asistencia”.

sources.body:
Sánchez y Feijóo, en el debate electoral de 2023. / Eduardo Parra - Europa Press

Alberto Núñez Feijóo acepta ahora un debate a cuatro en televisión con Pedro Sánchez, Santiago Abascal y el candidato que designe el espacio a la izquierda del PSOE, además de otro cara a cara con el presidente del Gobierno durante la campaña del próximo mes de noviembre para las elecciones del 29-N. El líder del Partido Popular (PP) rectifica así su decisión de la última campaña en julio de 2023, cuando dejó vacía la silla de un debate en Radio Televisión Española (RTVE) que finalmente fue a tres, entre Sánchez, el líder de Vox y la vicepresidenta Yolanda Díaz, entonces candidata de Sumar.

En un comunicado remitido a los medios, el PP informa de que acepta la oferta de Mediaset para celebrar ese cara a cara con Sánchez, el formato habitual entre los dos únicos candidatos con posibilidades de llegar a La Moncloa, y otra de Atresmedia para el citado debate a cuatro . Nada dice de debatir en RTVE, aunque sobre el Ente público afirma que Feijóo será entrevistado allí, pero no en los programas de información política y tertulia que se realizan con producción externa, como Mañaneros, presentado por Jesús Cintora, Directo al Grano o Malas Lenguas, conducido por Esther Palomera y Gonzalo Miró , sino en los de producción propia. Algo que permite que otro de los principales rostros de la cadena, Silvia Intxaurrondo, le entreviste en su programa La Hora de la 1, como ya ocurrió en 2023, aunque también podría hacerlo la presentadora de la segunda edición del telediario, Pepa Bueno.

El primer partido de la oposición habla incluso de fechas para esos posibles debates. El cara a cara con Sánchez el primer lunes de la campaña, día 16 de noviembre, y el debate a cuatro el jueves 26 de noviembre, penúltimo día de la campaña. Sí que se acepta, como es habitual, un debate en RTVE con todas las fuerzas con representación parlamentaria , propuesto para el 23 de noviembre, al que no acuden los primeros espadas de la carrera electoral, salvo en los grupos minoritarios. En el caso del PP, quien intervendrá en el debate será la portavoz parlamentaria, Ester Muñoz.

El comunicado del comité de campaña de los populares -constituido tras la Junta Directiva Nacional celebrada este jueves y con el secretario general del partido, Miguel Tellado, al mando- no ahorra críticas a la radio televisión pública y a sus directivos, aunque no cita al presidente, José Pablo López . Unas críticas que no son inéditas en el PP, que reitera que "la Compañía no tiene directivos que trabajen pensando en el interés general, pero sí magníficos profesionales de la comunicación. Deben ser ellos y no una productora externa quienes asuman el reto y la responsabilidad de organizar estas entrevistas, tan importantes, tanto en TVE como en RNE [Radio Nacional de España]".

Por si quedase alguna duda, el PP la despeja: "Si RTVE cumple con esta premisa, Feijóo irá". Los populares desarrollan así su postura: "Pese a la innegable parcialidad y sumisión a los intereses de la dirección de RTVE a las necesidades del presidente del Gobierno, Alberto Núñez Feijóo asistirá con la condición de que la entrevista se desarrolle en un espacio de producción propia". Fuentes del PP precisan que la entrevista a su candidato podría hacerla uno de los presentadores estrella que no forman parte de la plantilla del Ente público, siempre y cuando, precisan, la producción de la entrevista corra a cargo de los profesionales de la casa.

El Banco de España ha advertido que la construcción de vivienda no está creciendo tanto como se necesitaría para cubrir la demanda, en medio de la crisis de precios para alquilar o comprar una casa. El avance "más moderado de lo previsto" en la inversión residencial se debe a que falta mano de obra y suelo finalista , y a que sobra burocracia, que ralentiza los desarrollos urbanísticos.

Así lo recoge en el informe de proyecciones macroeconómicas y de la economía española del tercer trimestre, que se ha publicado este viernes y en el que ha mejorado en tres décimas la perspectiva de crecimiento del producto interior bruto (PIB) este año, hasta el 2,6% , a pesar de que anticipa un invierno de facturas de la luz y el gas elevadas por el conflicto en Oriente Medio.

El Banco de España vuelve a explicar el "aumento sostenido" de los precios de la vivienda con la escasez de nuevas casas para los hogares creados en los últimos años. Sus analistas cifran el déficit en torno a los 750.000, pero advierten que se acercará al millón en los próximos dos años.

Esa circunstancia debería animar a las empresas a invertir en este sector, pero ¿por qué persiste la "rigidez" en la oferta, cuando, además, la financiación bancaria ha mejorado para la construcción y la promoción inmobiliaria?

El número de viviendas iniciadas ha aumentado desde 2024, pero el avance se ha moderado en 2026: se registra un menor ritmo en la ejecución de los visados, menor tasa de casas terminadas , mayores costes productivos y más dificultades para conectarse a la red eléctrica , lo que limita las nuevas promociones, según enumera el documento.

El Banco de España señala que la evolución de los próximos ejercicios es clave y dependerá de si persisten los problemas estructurales de falta de mano de obra, lentitud en los desarrollos urbanísticos y escasez de suelo finalista, teniendo en cuenta que el tiempo medio de construcción es de casi tres años.

Asimismo, subraya que los programas públicos para construir vivienda protegida, sean del Estado, las autonomías o los ayuntamientos, pueden impulsar la inversión residencial a partir de 2027.

El dinamismo del sector en general tendrá peso en el crecimiento de la economía en los próximos meses.

Como avanzábamos, en este mismo informe, el Banco de España ha mejorado la previsión de crecimiento de la economía española hasta el 2,6% este año y el 2,2% el que viene, esto es, tres y cinco décimas más que en su último cálculo publicado en junio.

Esto ocurre a pesar del "complejo contexto internacional" y del "encarecimiento de la energía" desde el cierre del estrecho de Ormuz por la guerra en Irán. Según su análisis, el alza del PIB español se ha apoyado en el consumo privado, la creación de empleo y el aumento de la población "por el impulso de la inmigración ".

Pero, en paralelo, las últimas proyecciones del Banco de España arrojan un aumento de la inflación hasta el 3,9% este año y el 3,7% en el próximo, tras revisar al alza en tres décimas y en 1,1 puntos porcentuales las tasas de 2026 y 2027, respectivamente. Este escenario mejorará si se resuelve el conflicto en Oriente Medio de forma diplomática, pero empeorará si aumenta la tensión geopolítica.

sources.headline: El juez Pedraz rechaza imputar “en este momento” al PSOE en el ‘caso Leire Díez’, como pedía el PP

sources.body:
La sede del PSOE de la calle Ferraz de Madrid

El juez de la Audiencia Nacional Santiago Pedraz ha rechazado “de momento” imputar al PSOE en el llamado caso Leire. El magistrado ha dictado un auto esta mañana por el que acuerda practicar nuevas diligencias, ya que “actualmente no existe un principio de prueba suficiente que demuestre deficiencias estructurales de control o un beneficio directo para la organización”. Pedraz se adscribe así a las tesis de la Fiscalía anticorrupción, que ayer abogó por no dar por ahora al partido socialista la categoría de investigado.

La decisión de Pedraz se produce después de que la acusación popular solicitase la imputación del PSOE al considerar que el partido está detrás de la trama de Leire Díez, la llamada fontanera del PSOE, que habría tratado de “desestabilizar de forma sistemática y continuada cualquier procedimiento judicial u actuación policial que pudiera impactar directa o indirectamente en los intereses del PSOE o del Gobierno, gravemente afectados en ese momento por la consecutiva apertura de procedimientos judiciales en los que se investigaba a miembros de partido o de la familia del presidente del Gobierno”.

La acusación popular, que pedía que se investigase al PSOE por los presuntos delitos de cohecho, tráfico de influencias, blanqueo de capitales, malversación y financiación ilegal de partidos políticos, se refería a casos como los de David Sánchez, hermano de Pedro Sánchez. La jueza instructora del asunto, Beatriz Biedma, fue presuntamente acosada por esta presunta trama. Biedma declaró ayer como testigo en la Audiencia Nacional.

No obstante, Pedraz no ha admitido la solicitud de la acusación al considerar que en este momento “no se acredita lo que se viene denominando un principio de prueba para atribuir la condición de investigado”, aun cuando “los hechos pudieran presentar en abstracto apariencia delictiva por parte del PSOE”. El juez recuerda que para dar la condición de investigado al PSOE es imprescindible probar aspectos como un “defecto estructural de organización, control y supervisión dentro de la entidad” y la existencia de un “beneficio directo o indirecto para la organización”. Algo que de momento no se ha contrastado.

En consecuencia, el magistrado indica que será necesario practicar nuevas diligencias, tales como el “análisis de la documentación incautada en la sede y en el domicilio de Santos Cerdán”, ex secretario de Organización del PSOE y presunto líder de la trama, para poder decidir en el futuro si atribuye al PSOE la condición de persona jurídica investigada .

stories.headline: Bank of Spain raises its 2026 growth forecast but expects elevated inflation driven by energy prices

sources.body:
El consumo y las exportaciones sostienen la actividad

El organismo mejora en tres y cinco décimas sus estimaciones del PIB para este año y el próximo, mientras revisa al alza los precios hasta el 3,9% y el 3,7% por la guerra en Oriente Próximo

Un detalle de la fachada del Banco de España.

El Banco de España ha revisado este viernes al alza sus previsiones de crecimiento de la economía española para este año y el próximo, pero también ha empeorado significativamente sus perspectivas de inflación. El organismo calcula ahora que el producto interior bruto (PIB) avanzará un 2,6% en 2026 y un 2,2% en 2027, lo que supone tres y cinco décimas más, respectivamente, que en sus estimaciones de junio. Al mismo tiempo, eleva la inflación prevista hasta el 3,9% este ejercicio y el 3,7% el siguiente, tres décimas y 1,1 puntos porcentuales por encima de sus anteriores pronósticos.

Así se desprende del informe trimestral de la economía española correspondiente al tercer trimestre de 2026, en el que la institución constata la resistencia de la actividad económica frente a las consecuencias de la guerra en Oriente Próximo y el encarecimiento de la energía. La fortaleza del consumo privado, las exportaciones y el crecimiento de la población permitirán mantener este año el mismo ritmo de expansión registrado en 2025, aunque el organismo advierte de una aceleración de los precios que amenaza con prolongarse durante 2027.

La mejora de las previsiones responde, fundamentalmente, al comportamiento de la economía durante la primera mitad del año. El PIB creció un 0,7% trimestral entre abril y junio , frente al 0,6% del primer trimestre y por encima de lo anticipado. Los indicadores disponibles apuntan, además, a un nuevo avance del 0,6% en el tercer trimestre. Este mayor dinamismo también explica la revisión al alza de las perspectivas para 2027, pese a unas condiciones financieras y un entorno internacional menos favorables.

El consumo de los hogares continuará siendo el principal motor económico. El Banco de España estima que aumentará un 3% en 2026 , frente al 3,1% del año anterior, antes de moderarse hasta el 1,9% en 2027. El avance del empleo, la población y la renta disponible sostiene el gasto de las familias, que disponen también de un colchón de ahorro para amortiguar el impacto del encarecimiento de los productos y de los tipos de interés.

Sin embargo, la inflación constituye el principal contrapunto a estas perspectivas de crecimiento. El índice armonizado de precios de consumo pasó del 3,5% en abril al 5% en septiembre, según el indicador adelantado, impulsado especialmente por la energía. Los precios energéticos registraron una subida interanual del 22% en septiembre , quince puntos más que en abril, mientras los servicios mantienen aumentos persistentes ligeramente superiores al 4%.

El organismo prevé que la inflación permanezca en el entorno del 5% hacia finales de 2026 , incluso teniendo en cuenta las medidas fiscales destinadas a contener los precios energéticos. A principios de 2027 anticipa otro repunte, asociado a la desaparición de las rebajas fiscales sobre la energía y de los descuentos al transporte público. Posteriormente comenzaría una moderación gradual que dejaría la inflación media del próximo año en el 3,7%, todavía muy por encima del objetivo del 2% del Banco Central Europeo.
sources.headline: El Banco de España eleva el crecimiento al 2,6% en 2026 y anticipa ya dos años de inflación elevada

sources.body:
El precio de las gasolinas sigue aumentando

El Banco de España ratifica que el comportamiento de la economía española viene determinado por dos factores: un crecimiento que sigue resiliente, hasta el 2,6% este año; y al mismo tiempo, una inversión disparada, que se eleva hasta el 3,9%, que seguirá muy alta en el 2027, hasta el 3,7%, y además que sigue aumentando la brecha con la registrada en la zona euro, que queda muy por debajo.

Los precios de la energía, que han subido de una manera generalizada, son los principales responsables de este aumento de la inflación. Aquí se suman los incrementos del precio del gas a nivel internacional y el encarecimiento del petróleo y de los márgenes de refino, lo que afecta especialmente al gasóleo. De esta manera, el Banco de España ha revisado tres décimas al alza su previsión de junio, hasta el citado 3,9% de inflación para este año por los precios de la energía, mientras que, en cambio, los precios de los alimentos se han modificado a la baja. Una tasa que podría incrementarse en dos décimas más, hasta el 4,1 % si hay repunte de tensiones geopolíticas. Y con la presión de los precios manteniéndose en el 2027, cuando solo se moderaría dos décimas, manteniéndose en un elevado 3,7%.

Este aumento de la inflación ha sido más pronunciado en España que en la zona euro, de manera que se ha ampliado la brecha entre las dos zonas, que estaba en 0,5 puntos porcentuales en abril y que en septiembre ya ha llegado a 1,2 puntos. Desde mediados de 2025, los precios de consumo han crecido en España de forma persistente por encima de los de la zona euro y se han incrementado de manera muy destacada desde el estallido de la guerra de Irán. La razón principal del aumento de la diferencia viene por los precios energéticos, pero también por los del turismo y la hostelería, que en España han subido a mayor ritmo y que además pesan más en la cesta de la compra.

Los tres paquetes de medidas adoptados por el Gobierno para frenar la inflación tienen sus efectos frenando el aumento, pero también un coste. El Banco de España lo sitúa en el 0,52% del PIB, repartido entre un impacto mayor del primer bloque, de marzo a junio, que se lleva más de la mitad, y más reducido de los adoptados en junio y septiembre.

Mientras sufrimos con la inflación, el crecimiento mantiene su buen comportamiento, de manera que el Banco de España ha aumentado tres décimas su anterior previsión hasta dejarla en el 2,6%, la misma que tiene el Gobierno. Las causas son la fortaleza del consumo privado, la creación de empleo y el crecimiento de la población. El gasto de los hogares se mantendrá en los próximos meses gracias en parte a que la tasa de ahorro sigue en niveles elevados, mientras que las ratios de endeudamiento están contenidos.

El comportamiento del mercado de trabajo viene marcado por el proceso de regularización de extranjeros, que crecieron un 17,7% interanual en septiembre por la incorporación a la Seguridad Social de 421.000 afiliados beneficiarios de este proceso. Mientras, la tasa de paro seguirá descendiendo, marcando un 10% este año y un 9,7% el próximo.

stories.headline: Barcelona moves to raise property tax on tourist flats by as much as 150% before their planned phaseout

sources.body: La idea és el que el 2028 desapareguin a Barcelona , però fins llavors, el govern de Jaume Collboni cosirà a impostos als pisos turístics . Ho va anunciar dimarts el tinent d’alcaldia d’Economia, Jordi Valls, i aquest divendres la Comissió d’Economia i Hisenda de l’Ajuntament de Barcelona hi ha donat llum verda . En una sessió extraordinària, s’ha aprovat modificar les ordenances fiscals del 2027 per apujar-los l’IBI fins al 150 % . La mesura ha tirat endavant amb els vots del PSC, BComú i ERC, mentre que el PP i Vox hi han votat en contra i Junts s’ha abstingut. Encara faltarà l’aprovació definitiva, que previsiblement arribarà al plenari municipal del desembre . Un cop passi, ja el 2027 , els propietaris d’un sol pis turístic passaran a pagar un 50 % d’IBI; els qui en tinguin entre 2 i 4, un 100 % i els qui en tinguin més de quatre hauran de pagar el màxim que permet la llei, un 150 %. El consistori pot aplicar l’encariment d’aquest impost perquè així ho permeten els decrets d’habitatge impulsats pel Govern espanyol. També et pot interessar Pedro Sánchez troba una via alternativa per aprovar els decrets d’habitatge tombats pel Congrés Marina Segura i Vidal 1 minut de lectura Un pis “no és un actiu econòmic” Durant la seva intervenció, el tinent Valls ha defensat que continuaran aplicant totes les eines al seu abast “per dificultar el desenvolupament d’usos turístics en habitatges “, perquè considera que un habitatge “és una llar” i “ no és un actiu econòmic “. Segons ha detallat, els propietaris d’aquests pisos tendeixen a una “ acumulació de les llicències “. En concret, el 60 % n’ acumulen quatre o més . Els càlculs de l’executiu socialista apunten que amb l’augment d’aquest impost es podran recaptar uns 7 M€ cada any, que volen destinar a la promoció d’habitatge protegit . Una mesura curta per a uns, excessiva per a d’altres Els comuns han demanat al govern anar un pas més enllà i encarir l’IBI també als propietaris de més d’un pis . “El problema que tenim no és de l’habitatge turístic, el problema que tenim és l’ especulació “, ha denunciat el portaveu Marc Serra. ERC ha estat molt clara a l’hora de demanar a l’Ajuntament en què s’ha d’invertir el que es recapti d’aquesta pujada: “Volem tenir el compromís que anirà a ampliar el parc de lloguer públic de la ciutat”, ha dit la regidora Rosa Suriñach. A l’altra cara de la moneda, Arnau Vives ( Junts ) ha alertat que la mesura “incrementa la recaptació, però no garanteix un millor accés al mercat de lloguer “. Víctor Martí ( PP ) ha criticat que suposa una “ estocada fiscal “. “Una cosa és regular una activitat econòmica i una altra és utilitzar la fiscalitat com a instrument de càstig “, ha dit. Gonzalo de Oro ( Vox ), en la mateixa línia, ha assegurat que aquest expedient “destapa la verdadera cara del govern: la improvisació , l’ afany recaptatori , el cinisme polític i el populisme “.
